general_information.Description: This course introduces students to the end to end machine learning lifecycle, focusing on the practices, tools, and culture of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps). Students will learn how to transition machine learning models from isolated experimental notebooks into production-ready, scalable, and continuously monitored software systems. The curriculum covers project scoping, data version control (DVC), automated data and model pipelines (TFX), containerization (Docker), continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD), model serving architectures, and automated drift monitoring. By completing hands-on labs and a final capstone project, students will gain engineering skills to build reliable, reproducible, and automated AI systems.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, and labs assigned by the instructor in class or at home, and submitting them on time. - Laptops are to be used in class strictly for learning purposes. - Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
general_information.Tools: Python, Git, Docker, DVC, TFX (TensorFlow Extended), MLflow, FastAPI, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, Evidently AI.
general_information.Note: - The course emphasizes a semester-long MLOps capstone project, where students progressively design, implement, deploy, and monitor a real-world machine learning system following industry-standard MLOps practices. The project is developed through four milestone reports aligned with the MLOps lifecycle. - The final mark is determined by summing the weighted scores of: Progress Test 1 (10%), Report 1 – Project Scoping & Lifecycle Design (10%), Report 2 – Data Pipeline & Reproducibility Setup (10%), Report 3 – Automated Pipeline & Model Testing (30%), Report 4 – Model Serving & Active Monitoring (10%), and Final Exam (30%). - The four project reports progressively evaluate students' ability to: - define and scope an ML problem and design its lifecycle; - build reproducible data pipelines with version control and experiment tracking; - implement automated ML pipelines with testing and continuous integration; - deploy, monitor, and maintain production-ready ML services using modern MLOps tools. - The final examination is a computer-based multiple-choice examination covering the theoretical and practical foundations of MLOps across the entire course, including ML lifecycle management, data engineering, reproducibility, pipeline automation, deployment, CI/CD, monitoring, and operational excellence. - Completion Criteria: every assessment component > 0 AND Final Exam Score ≥ 4.0 AND Final Result ≥ 5.0.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the core concepts of the MLOps lifecycle, maturity models, and the fundamental architectural differences between DevOps, DataOps, and MLOps.
Execute machine learning project scoping, define business key performance indicators (KPIs), select appropriate deployment patterns, and establish reliable performance baselines.
Implement systematic error analysis, data-centric AI techniques, and experiment tracking to address issues like skewed datasets and class imbalance.
Build automated data pipelines utilizing version control tools (DVC) and centralized feature stores (TFX) to guarantee data lineage and experiment reproducibility.
Design and coordinate end-to-end machine learning orchestration pipelines utilizing components like TensorFlow Extended (TFX) for training, evaluation, and validation.
Apply containerization (Docker) and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) workflows to automate model testing and infrastructure provisioning.
Deploy production-grade model serving microservices using architectures like FastAPI, TensorFlow Serving, and Kubernetes supporting progressive delivery patterns.
Construct automated production monitoring infrastructures with Prometheus, Grafana, and Evidently AI to detect data drift, concept drift, and performance degradation.
Architect, document, and present a complete, end-to-end operational MLOps system that solves a real-world enterprise problem.
